---
title: "Data"
---

The data output from the laboratory assays is complex.

Here is a common example of information from patient sampling that you might end up with
Sometimes this

1. Patient demographic data
2. Patient survey
3. Sample information
4. Processed results for sample from laboratory assays


You may also need to consider you have

- Multiple samples collected from the same person
- Multiple sampling timepoints - 
- Various nuances in analysing the laboratory data - not all of the following will apply to all assays and nomenclature varies alot!
    - Positive controls - this may be in the form of a sample with pathogen present
    - Negative controls - may be in the form of a sample with pathogen present, or maybe a 
    - Blank control - used for analytical purposes to ensure no 'back ground' interference 
    - Reference samples
    - Long-term reference samples - ensure stability of assays being performed,
